notable_absence.finding: This page is the corpus's only stated definition of 'the Couchbase Data Model' as a named thing (title: 'The Couchbase Data Model'), yet nothing in the registry previously modeled schema flexibility, or the document-versus-relational comparison, at all - directly confirming the round's stated hole ('the document data model is absent entirely'). Notably the page never once mentions scope or collection, even though data.md (this batch's page 1) ties every item to 'its bucket' - the data-model page and the data-organization page (scopes-and-collections.md, this batch's page 3) are documented as two entirely separate topics with no cross-link between them on either page.

cross_component_finding: The page states Couchbase 'does not enforce uniformity' and that schemas are 'entirely defined and managed by applications' - a foundational claim for how n1ql:select and n1ql:create-index behave against heterogeneous documents (e.g. why CREATE INDEX often targets one specific attribute path rather than a table-wide column), but no promoted n1ql:* relation in the registry currently states that dependency explicitly; SQL++'s reference pages document syntax, not the schema-less premise underneath it.
cross_product_finding: This page discusses only the document-versus-relational comparison and never mentions Capella, Sync Gateway, Couchbase Lite, or any other Couchbase product - unlike data.md and scopes-and-collections.md in the same directory, it has no cross-product angle to report.
